_discipline: Each seed MUST produce a non-empty primary response. If the audit reports EMPTY for a chain whose source-side returned data, that's a chain failure — not a data-availability false negative. Update seeds in this file when an upstream entity is deleted; otherwise leave alone.
_provenance: All seeds verified live against hansard-api / legislation.gov.uk / TNA Find Case Law on 2026-05-29. The Lords division ext_ids are from the Renters' Rights Bill ping-pong of 14 Oct 2025 (3 known divisions on Motions A1/C1/H1).
_debate_ext_id_note: Renters' Rights Bill, Lords, 14 Oct 2025. Known to contain 3 divisions and many contributions (Lord Pannick et al). Exercises divisions chain + contribution drill-down.
_member_id_note: 62 = Lord Whitehead (now Minister of State, DESNZ — known to have governmentPosts and oppositionPosts in biography). 4514 = Sir Keir Starmer (current PM — extensive Hansard record).
_contribution_ext_id_note: Baroness Bowles, Financial Services and Markets Bill, 25 Jan 2023 (verified live in PR #18 smoke tests). Exercises hansard://debate/{ext}/contribution/{ext} resource.
_judgment_slug_note: A real TNA Find Case Law judgment. Exercises judgment://{slug*}/{header,index,para/{eId}} resource family. Returns LegalDocML XML.
_legislation_triple_note: Housing Act 1988 s.21 (the section we've been smoke-testing for extent + Repeal detection). Exercises legislation_get_section + legislation_get_toc + legislation://{type}/{year}/{number}/section/{section} resource.
_column_volume_house_note: Lord Pannick's Motion C1 citation from the Renters' Rights debate. Vol 849 is Source:2 DailyHansard (a Daily Part, NOT a Bound Volume) yet resolves cleanly — proves column resolution is not gated on publication state. Exercises parliament_lookup_by_column.
_topic_phrase_note: High-volume topic (61,609 Hansard hits as of 2026-05-29). Used to exercise parliament_search_hansard and verify the corpus envelope (top_debates, top_divisions, totals) is populated.
_petition_id_note: Empty — we don't currently have a stable seed. The petitions module's chains are exercised via petition.parliament.uk live queries instead. Add a seed if a stable open petition becomes a target.
